teaser.en: A smooth-barked timber tree common in the coast's forests, with leaflets that are lopsided, one side wider than the other.

summary.en: *Mkuwa* is a buttressed, smooth-barked tree of coastal woodland and forest, and one of the common coastal forest trees used for timber.

about.en: *Mkuwa* usually has a buttressed trunk and smooth grey bark. The leaves have two or three pairs of leaflets, and each leaflet is asymmetric, with one side wider than the other. The fruits are oblong pods, as in other members of the bean family.

where.en: It grows in *Brachystegia* woodland, along the edges of creeks, and in evergreen and riverine forest.

uses.en: *Mkuwa* is one of the common coastal forest trees, and it is used as timber.

names.en: Pakia records two Digo names, *mkuwa* and *ukwe*; the ICRAF handbook gives *mkue*. In Swahili it is *mkue* or *mukuwa*, and in Giriama *msahe*. The Swahili *mkue* is also used for *Paramacrolobium coeruleum*, which the Digo call *mrihi* or *mukwe*, so these names overlap between trees.

reason.en: Brachystegia, the woodland it grows in
Major timber tree of the same family
